ai.title: Add Notion query and researcher agents
ai.summary: New `notion-query-agent` and `notion-researcher` definitions added to `.agents/`. Both use `x-ai/grok-4-fast` and connect to `@notionhq/notion-mcp-server`. The researcher orchestrates parallel spawning of query agents via `spawn_agents` tool.

eli5.text: A new research assistant can now search through your Notion notes and documents and find answers to specific questions, while a second assistant coordinates it by breaking big research topics into smaller questions and running those searches in parallel. These assistants are defined in two new configuration files that were added, and both connect to Notion using a shared integration token. If you looked at the files, you'd see the first is a specialized search tool that knows how to read Notion databases and pages, and the second is a coordinator that can spawn multiple instances of the search tool at once to gather information faster. This is live today for anyone using the internal agent system.

ai.title: Update SDK README examples
ai.summary: Updated sdk/README.md to use versioned agent IDs (codebuff/base@0.0.16) and changed the custom agent model example to x-ai/grok-4-fast. Added explicit toolNames field in AgentDefinition example and clarified custom agent/tool definition comments. Event logging examples now use JSON.stringify.

eli5.text: The examples in the software development kit guide now show you how to point at a specific published version of a helper (like codebuff/base@0.0.16) instead of a generic name, and the sample custom helper now uses a different artificial-intelligence model (x-ai/grok-4-fast). When you run the example code, the program will print detailed event information using JSON.stringify, making the output easier to read. These changes only affect the written instructions and do not alter any actual functionality today.

ai.title: Refine agent docs and tool type definitions
ai.summary: Updated custom agent documentation and type definitions to reflect current tooling. Removed deprecated planning and output control tools from type unions, consolidating `FileTools` into `FileEditingTools` and `TerminalTools`. Adjusted MCP config schemas to include `headers` in stdio transport. Revised template comments and model defaults in `my-custom-agent.ts` to align with active model versions like `x-ai/grok-4-fast`.

eli5.text: When you type `codebuff` at the command line, the placeholder file that used to greet new custom agents now shows up-to-date, simpler instructions written in plain commands you can copy and paste. Behind the scenes, the list of allowed AI helper tools was pared down, some older planning and output-control tools that nothing calls anymore were dropped, a couple of remaining tool groups were folded into broader, easier-to-read categories, and the configuration for connecting external services like Notion now lets you add private headers when running on your own computer. The bundled agent template also switched its default AI model from the previous recommended model to x-ai/grok-4-fast. These changes are live today wherever you download the latest version of codebuff.

ai.title: Dynamic Agent Definition Docs
ai.summary: Docs now load `AgentDefinition.ts` content dynamically via `/api/docs/agent-definition`. Replaced static schema display with `AgentDefinitionDisplay` component in `agent-reference.mdx`. New route reads `common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/types/agent-definition.ts` directly. `Logger` type import moved to `util-types` in `agent-template.ts`.

eli5.text: The agent reference page now pulls the actual TypeScript definition file live from the source code via a new internal endpoint, instead of showing a hand-maintained static copy that could drift out of sync. Anyone reading the docs on the website will see the current agent definition content automatically refreshed rather than a potentially outdated snapshot. Behind the scenes, the display component fetches and renders the freshly read source file on demand, so the documentation stays in step with the real code. This is live today and applies to the public-facing agent reference docs.
